forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: SHDC Q1 GF Capital Finance Report 2026-27 Appendix B
findings.headline: Capital programme forecast outturn £28.432m, underspend of £773k (2.6%) from £29.205m budget; underspends driven by lower demand
findings.detail: Q1 actual spending of £3.215m represents 11% of the revised full-year budget. Forecast outturn is £28.432m. Multiple schemes show underspends due to lower demand: Disabled Facilities Grants £143k under (grant exceeds demand), Neighbourhoods £364k under (reduced vehicle replacement need with cost savings found), and Health & Wellbeing Hub £232k under. These are demand-driven variations, not delivery constraints.
findings.matters: A lender would want to understand whether capital spending variations reflect delivery delays or demand fluctuations. Underspends driven by lower demand indicate the council is responsive to actual service needs and managing finances effectively.
findings.quote: SHDC have historically underspent DFGs as grant received outstrips demand.

findings.paper_title: SHDC Q1 GF Capital Finance Report 2026-27 Appendix B
findings.headline: Capital Enhancements schemes are largely on hold, with only the Spalding Cemetery Expansion proceeding in the current financial year.
findings.detail: The £184k Capital Enhancements budget is forecast to spend only £150k, indicating that schemes other than the cemetery expansion have been deferred. The document does not explain the reasons for deferral or planned timings for the deferred schemes.
findings.matters: Although the Capital Enhancements budget is small relative to the total programme (£184k of £29.2m), the deferral of multiple schemes may indicate resource constraints or other factors a lender would want to understand.
findings.quote: Capital Enhancements – Spalding Cemetery Expansion only scheme currently forecast to be moving forward within current financial year with other schemes on hold.

findings.paper_title: SHDC Q1 GF Capital Finance Report 2026-27 Appendix B
findings.headline: The £16.708m Health & Wellbeing Hub, representing 57% of the capital programme, is progressing on track for early 2027 completion and opening.
findings.detail: By end Q1, the project had spent £2.747m of a forecast total of £16.476m. The document reports positive physical progress including pool tank formation and testing, internal configuration progressing, and contractor appointment imminent for the 3G pitch. The project is forecast to complete with a minor £232k underspend.
findings.matters: The Health & Wellbeing Hub is by far the largest capital investment in the council's programme. A lender would monitor the council's ability to deliver major projects on schedule, and positive progress confirms adequate project governance and delivery capability.
findings.quote: Positive progress continues. New pool tanks are formed and being tested for water tightness. New internal configuration taking shape. Tenders for 3G pitch construction completed to enable contractor appointment. Scheme progress is on track for early 2027 completion and opening.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A Q1 SHDC Performance Report
findings.headline: Business rates and Council tax in-year collection both ahead of quarterly profile.
findings.detail: Business rates in-year collection rate is 30.37% against a 28.00% target. Council tax in-year collection rate is 28.64% against a 28.50% target. Both are performing ahead of quarterly profile, indicating strong early-year revenue generation and cash flow.
findings.matters: Strong collection ahead of profile indicates healthy cash flow and residents' ability to pay. Early outperformance provides financial flexibility and reduces revenue shortfall risk.
findings.figures: Business Rates: 30.37% vs 28.00% target (marked J); Council Tax: 28.64% vs 28.50% target (marked J)

findings.paper_title: Appendix A Q1 SHDC Performance Report
findings.headline: Sports Centre closed September 2025; council now operates from temporary facility with reduced capacity.
findings.detail: The Sports Centre closed in September 2025 and the council is currently delivering leisure services from a temporary facility with reduced capacity, limited equipment, and restricted activity program. Several dryside activities and bowls are unavailable. Despite constraints, participation has been maintained relatively well.
findings.matters: Closure of a major asset indicates capital pressures or planned works. Ongoing operation from temporary facilities carries higher interim costs and risks extended service disruption, affecting debt repayment capacity.
findings.figures: Visitor numbers Q1: 27,547 (vs 84,226 in Q1 prior year); gym members: 845; swimming lesson participation: 19,433
findings.quote: Since the Sports Centre closed in September 2025, performance has remained strong despite operating from a temporary facility with reduced capacity, limited equipment, and a restricted activity programme.
